entities.summary: Edna Pauline Plumstead was a South African palaeobotanist, of the Bernard Price Institute for Palaeontological Research, University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, where she graduated in 1924. Edna lived in Cape Town the first seven years of her life and that is where she would explore and find wild flowers in the Cape Peninsula. Plumstead would later on connect the wild flowers to the same one in places like Australia and South America when she would later on defend the continental drift. She first began defending the theory of continental drift in the 1950s and has been described as one 'of South Africa's foremost scientists in the field of Gondwana paleobotany and geology'.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Edna Plumstead's work on Gondwana paleobotany and geology contributed significantly to the understanding of continental drift, a theory that has had far-reaching implications for our understanding of Earth's history and evolution.
